The Thunder had a perfect start to the season, picking up double-digit wins over the Spurs and Nuggets. But then Jalen Williams suffered a gruesome right leg injury late in their win over the Clippers on Sunday.

Two takeaways

  • The defense has been terrific, with the Nuggets’ 84 points on 94 possessions on Thursday being a worse offensive performance than any that they had last season. The Thunder have somehow allowed just 77 per 100 in Alex Caruso’s 67 minutes on the floor, and his 7.5 deflections per 36 minutes rank fourth among 210 players who’ve logged at least 50 minutes total.
  • The offense has been sub-par, though the Thunder have scored plenty efficiently with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on the floor. They’ve scored just 57 on 77 (74 per 100) with him off the floor, and the lack of Williams for an extended period certainly won’t help in that regard.

Coming up: The Thunder were just 7-7 in the second games of back-to-backs last season, but they’re one of three teams with a league-low seven rest-disadvantage games this year. The first is Monday against the Suns, after which they’ll play 12 of their next 17 games on the road.

Week 2: vs. PHX, @ DAL, @ HOU

Record: 3-0

OffRtg: 118.7 (6) DefRtg: 106.4 (7) NetRtg: +12.4 (5)

The Pistons had the best record (18-7) in games played between Eastern Conference playoff teams last season, and they’ve begun the new year with impressive wins over the Celtics, Heat and Sixers. They had a rest advantage for their wire-to-wire victory in Philadelphia on Sunday, but were without Jalen Duren (out at least two weeks) and Ausar Thompson (ankle sprain).

Two takeaways

  • The Pistons made 14 or more 3-pointers in only 20 (24%) of their 82 games last season, but they’ve made at least 14 in all three games this year. They’ve seen the league’s second biggest jump in 3-point rate (from 35% to 43% of their shots), and they’ve shot 42.0% (third best) from beyond the arc, with Duncan Robinson 15-for-28 (54%).
  • The defense hasn’t been quite as tenacious as it was last season. That’s resulted in the league’s biggest drop in opponent turnover rate, but also its biggest drop in opponent free throw rate. Duren committed just two fouls in his 38 minutes against the Celtics and Heat.

Coming up: The Pistons swept the Knicks last season (winning the three games by an average of 28 points), but didn’t get a chance of facing the champs in the playoffs. They’ll play (at least) four times this year, with the first meeting at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday.

The Wolves are the second team in NBA history (joining the 2004-05 Jazz) to win each of their first three games by more than 20 points. And the third of those wins came against a team (Toronto) that had won its first two games by a total of 53.

Two takeaways

  • The Wolves have the league’s No. 1 defense, and the defense has been at its best (81.2 points allowed per 100 possessions) with LaMelo Ball on the floor. His minutes have been limited (22.8 per game) and 68% of them have come alongside both Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert. But Ball also leads the team with 4.8 deflections per 36 minutes, up from 2.6 with the Hornets last season.
  • They dominated the possession game in Miami and Orlando, producing the two biggest shot-opportunity differentials (+18 and +19) for any team in Week 1. Things flipped in that regard (-12) against Toronto, but the Raptors shot 10-for-48 (21%) from outside the paint. The Wolves are still one of two teams (Portland is the other) that rank in the top five in both offensive and defensive rebounding percentage.

Coming up: The Wolves have just seven rest-disadvantage games (tied for fewest in the league) this season, but two of them are this week. Their win over the Raptors on Sunday was the start of their first stretch of five games in seven days.

Week 2: @ CLE, vs. GSW, vs. LAC*, @ SAS

OffRtg: 122.6 (3) DefRtg: 112.5 (17) NetRtg: +10.2 (9)

No team had a more impressive Week 1 than the Rockets. They clobbered the Mavs, edged the Spurs and beat the 2-0 Hawks on the road. We may have already seen the defensive play of the year, with Amen Thompson blocking Victor Wembanyama’s layup in the final seconds on Friday.

Two takeaways

  • The offense is off to a hot start, with the Rockets the only team that ranks in the top five in field goal percentage, 3-point percentage and free throw percentage. They also scored 13 points on nine clutch possessions against the Spurs on Friday, with Alperen Sengun scoring or assisting on 11 of the 13.
  • Fred VanVleet (who sat out the second game of the weekend back-to-back) is just 6-for-18 from the field and isn’t getting them into their offense much faster. But he has 16 assists and zero turnovers. Overall, the Rockets’ turnover rate (15.9 per 100 possessions) is a little higher than it was last season (15.7 per 100), but the league-wide rate is way up (it’s early) and Houston’s rate has been much lower (14.6 per 100) in VanVleet’s 61 minutes on the floor.

Coming up: The Rockets and Hawks will be the first teams done playing each other this season, with their home-and-home set concluding in Houston on Monday. The Rockets will be at a rest disadvantage when they face the Thunder for the first time (Saturday in Houston).

Week 2: vs. ATL, @ MIL, @ DAL, vs. OKC

OffRtg: 105.5 (26) DefRtg: 102.4 (5) NetRtg: +3.1 (12)

The new-and-improved Sixers got off to a great start, going 3-0 (with wins over the Knicks and Cavs) before suffering a rest-disadvantage loss (without two starters) to the Pistons on Sunday. In their first back-to-back, they sat LeBron James in one game and Joel Embiid in the other.

Two takeaways

  • While offense is the greater curiosity, defense is the greater concern with the Sixers’ new core. But their starting lineup allowed the Knicks and Cavs to score just 56 points on 74 defensive possessions (76 per 100), with some terrific rotations down the stretch in New York on Tuesday. Embiid remains a huge difference-maker on that end of the floor.
  • Alas, Adem Bona is the only other healthy center on the roster, and the Sixers started a frontline of James and Dean Wade against the Pistons (who were without Jalen Duren) on Sunday. Over the four games total, they played 30 minutes with neither Embiid nor Bona on the floor (James has been on for almost all of those), and they’ve been outscored by 14 points (allowing 75 on 60 defensive possessions) in those 30 minutes.

Coming up: The Sixers were the only team to play four games in Week 1, but they’ll now have two days off before visiting Indiana on Wednesday. Their second meeting with the Knicks will be the first Emirates NBA Cup game in East Group B, what should be the best group of the six.

Week 2: @ IND, vs. NYK*, @ CHA

OffRtg: 110.5 (14) DefRtg: 111.3 (14) NetRtg: -0.7 (14)

A season with big expectations got off to a rough start for Victor Wembanyama (1-for-13 against the Thunder) and the Spurs. After losing to Oklahoma City and Houston, they trailed the shorthanded Mavs (no Kyrie Irving or Cooper Flagg) late in the third quarter on Saturday before pulling away in the final 13 minutes.

Two takeaways

  • The Spurs’ new starting lineup played limited minutes (just 9.4 per game) and the results were mixed. It outscored the Thunder by 10 points on Tuesday, but scored an anemic 30 points on 45 offensive possessions (67 per 100) against the Rockets and Mavs over the weekend. The offense was at its best with last season’s starter (Julian Champagnie) on the floor.
  • Victor Wembanyama has struggled with his jump shot. Combining preseason and Week 1, he’s shot 2-for-11 from mid-range and 5-for-28 from beyond the arc. But the Spurs have allowed less than a point per possession with him on the floor, while allowing 133 per 100 with him on the bench.

Coming up: The Spurs’ win in Dallas over the weekend was the start of what seems like a pretty soft, 12-game stretch of schedule that should have them at or near the top of the West in mid-November. Minnesota is the toughest opponent on that stretch, but the Spurs will have a rest advantage when they host the Wolves on Saturday.

Week 2: vs. SAC, @ UTA, vs. MIN

The Lakers are taking advantage of a soft start to their schedule, though they had to overcome an 11-point deficit against the Clippers and dig out of an 18-point hole in Utah.

Two takeaways

  • The league’s No. 1 offense has been led by Luka Dončić, who scored 52 points in Utah on Sunday and has a usage rate of 41.8%, which would be the highest rate for any player in the 31 seasons of play-by-play data. Austin Reaves has averaged 26.7 points with a ridiculous true shooting percentage of 82.0%, the highest mark among the 48 players who averaged 20-plus in Week 1.
  • Walker Kessler (16.7 per game) has been nearly as efficient and, not surprisingly, the Lakers’ defense has been at its best (105.6 points allowed per 100 possessions) with him on the floor. His 10 dunks in his Lakers debut on Wednesday were more than he had all of last season (nine in five games) and are tied for the fourth most for any player in a game in the 31 seasons of play-by-play data. Only Shaquille O’Neal has had more.

Coming up: The Lakers are one of three teams with three sets of five games in seven days this season. The first begins Tuesday with a visit from the 2-0 Blazers, and they’ll be at a rest disadvantage at the Intuit Dome the following night.

Week 2: vs. POR, @ LAC, @ GSW*, vs. TOR

The Celtics had two big games in Week 1, they were both within five points in the last five minutes, and they split them. They blew a 22-point, second-half lead in Detroit and then held on to edge New York in their home opener.

Two takeaways

  • Jayson Tatum struggled (6-for-23 shooting) in Detroit, but he took over down the stretch against the Knicks, hitting three straight jumpers in the final 90 seconds to put the game away. He’s totaled 18 assists over the two games, but had just six free throw attempts to go with his 49 shots. The Celtics again rank in the bottom three in both free throw rate (28th) and the percentage of their shots that have come in the paint (30th).
  • They’re also one of three teams in the bottom five in both offensive and defensive rebounding percentage, with Mitchell Robinson yet to make a big impact on the glass. Neemias Queta played a few more minutes off the bench than Robinson did as a starter over the two games and was on the floor in clutch time both nights.

Coming up: The Celtics’ four-game homestand continues with two games against the Bulls sandwiching a rest-disadvantage game against the Nets. They were 5-5 (1-2 at home) in rest-disadvantage games last season and are one of three teams with a league-high 14 of them this year.

Two takeaways

  • Turnovers (44 through two games) have been an issue, even though the Cavs rank in the bottom five in ball movement and had just 18 assists on their 39 buckets in Philly.
